answer: Each identity grows a private vine from a scarce oasis compute root by locking non-fungible pigment that accrues only via sequential memory-hard proofs bound to that identity. Sybil clones cannot share accumulation: pigment dilutes across each vine so influence falls to 1/n, forcing the attacker to run n independent sequential processes that refuse pooling. Cost is super-linear as n identities need n dedicated sequential streams plus joint collateral slashed on correlated faults from the same oasis cluster.
